text: EX-99.1 2 q3fy27pr.htm EX-99.1 Document NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 • Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago • Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago • Vera Rubin NVL72, the most versatile and advanced computing platform ever built, has shipped SANTA CLARA, Calif.—Nov. 17, 2026― NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively. “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.” In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization. NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026. NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook. • GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be between 71.0% and 72.0%. • GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $11.0 billion and $10.7 billion, respectively. • For the full year fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates to be between 16.0% and 18.0%, excluding any discrete items and material changes to NVIDIA’s tax environment. Highlights Data Center • Third-quarter revenue was $107.6 billion, up 21% from the previous quarter and up 110% from a year ago. • Ramped production and began shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 — the fastest product ramp in the company’s history — with racks running at partners including CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius, and coming online soon at SpaceXSI. • Expanded the Vera Rubin cloud ecosystem, announcing general availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, general availability of Google Cloud’s Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances and the continued buildout of SpaceXSI’s infrastructure. • Announced Vera Rubin open architecture advances to help the industry scale faster, and revealed that Cisco, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Visionbay are joining many technology leaders advancing infrastructure for Vera Rubin. • Revealed that leading AI natives, cloud providers and neoclouds, including CoreWeave, Meta, Nebius, Nscale, OpenAI and Verda, are building with NVIDIA Vera CPUs to support the growing computing needs of businesses and developers, joining AWS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and SpaceXSI. • Expanded Anthropic’s access to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers, and continued to collaborate on design and engineering to optimize future NVIDIA architectures for Anthropic’s workloads. • Announced the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing — combining NVIDIA’s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science. • Introduced NVIDIA Rubin HPC, a new GPU in the Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. • Expanded collaboration with Meta on AI agent Muse and its family of models, with Meta planning expanded deployment of Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ networking and BlueField®-4 to scale training, inference and agents. • Introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery to accelerate infrastructure deployment. • Announced European ecosystem adoption of NVIDIA DSX™ to reduce AI factory power requirements and enable near-zero facility cooling water consumption. • Announced that NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training and Endpoints benchmark, and Vera Rubin NVL72 demonstrated leading inference performance in its MLPerf Inference preview debut. • Launched NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform and introduced the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, combining open source OpenShell software, Vera Rubin for model inference, Vera CPUs for agent execution and BlueField®-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry to independently monitor agent behavior and enforce security policies in silicon. • Announced an agreement to acquire Hugging Face to scale its platform and make intelligence more open, capable and accessible. • Announced plans with global supply chain partners, including Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries and Unimicron Technology Corporation, to scale critical manufacturing capabilities to meet demand for NVIDIA infrastructure. • Deepened partnership with MediaTek across cloud infrastructure, local computing and automotive, extending NVIDIA’s rack-scale platform to custom XPUs through NVIDIA NVLink Fusion™. • Announced plans with Cisco for USFP, a new optical-module form factor designed to increase bandwidth density and power efficiency for next-generation AI factory networks. • Announced collaboration with Australia’s data center ecosystem on infrastructure supporting a planned buildout of up to 2 gigawatts by 2027 for NVIDIA DSX AI factories. • Introduced NVIDIA Nemotron for Science to help researchers build specialized agents for scientific discovery, and collaborated with global healthcare and life sciences organizations to advance protein design, accelerate drug discovery and expand precision patient care. • Partnered with Palantir to bring sovereign AI intelligence and NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models to critical supply chains. • Partnered with Firebird to scale the company’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity. • Expanded the open source NVIDIA CUDA-Q™ platform with CUDA-Q Logical for fault-tolerant quantum computing development, and ran a record simulation of a fault-tolerant quantum processor on JUPITER at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre. Edge Computing • Third-quarter Edge Computing revenue was $8.2 billion, up 14% from the previous quarter and up 42% from a year ago. • Reinvented Windows PCs with NVIDIA RTX Spark™ laptops, now shipping from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface and MSI. • Launched NVIDIA DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27 and Hogwarts Legacy , bringing AI-powered, photorealistic lighting and materials to GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, GeForce NOW and RTX Spark, and coming soon to Where Winds Meet . • Expanded the NVIDIA local AI lineup with a new NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB model, bringing near-frontier AI capabilities to desktops at a more accessible price point, and accelerated leading AI models from NVIDIA Nemotron, Black Forest Labs, Liquid AI and Qwen for running AI agents locally, with expanded support for Hermes, OpenClaw and Perplexity. • Introduced new NVIDIA Alpamayo™ development tools and the NVIDIA Halos™ SAFE framework to help developers build and evaluate autonomous-driving systems. • Expanded partnerships with Mercedes-Benz and Volvo Cars to advance safe automated driving. • Announced European mobility leaders — including Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride — are showcasing NVIDIA Hyperion™ use cases for automated vehicles and future robotaxi fleets. • Advanced the NVIDIA Isaac™ robotics platform with new development tools, datasets and runtime, alongside Agile Robots’ introduction of a reference humanoid powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor™ and built on Isaac GR00T. • Expanded NVIDIA Cosmos™ with tools to train, evaluate and deploy world models for robotics, autonomous vehicles and industrial applications. • Advanced AI-RAN with Nokia and global telecom operators, including T-Mobile’s first AI-RAN call on a commercial network, bringing NVIDIA accelerated computing deeper into wireless networks. CFO Commentary Commentary on the quarter by Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer, is available at https://investor.nvidia.com. Conference Call and Webcast Information NVIDIA will conduct a conference call with analysts and investors to discuss its third quarter fiscal 2027 financial results and current financial prospects today at 2 p.m. Pacific time (5 p.m. Eastern time). A live webcast (listen-only mode) of the conference call will be accessible at NVIDIA’s investor relations website, https://investor.nvidia.com. The webcast will be recorded and available for replay until NVIDIA’s conference call to discuss its financial results for its fourth quarter and full fiscal 2027. Non-GAAP Measures To supplement NVIDIA’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. These non-GAAP measures include non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP other income (expense), net, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income, or earnings, per diluted share, and free cash flow. For NVIDIA’s investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, legal settlement costs, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA’s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense. Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. NVIDIA believes the presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures enhances the users’ overall understanding of the company’s historical financial performance. The presentation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the company’s financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and the company’s non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies. These platforms incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services to deliver unique value. Our platforms address large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center and Edge Computing. We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks. In the interim, we have provided a supplemental document with additional financial information on our investor website. Revenue Revenue for the third quarter was a record $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago and up 20% sequentially. Data Center revenue for the third quarter was a record $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago and up 21% sequentially. Our Hyperscale and AI Clouds, Industrial, & Enterprise platforms both grew substantially, driven by the introduction of our Rubin infrastructure, our fastest architecture ramp ever, standalone Vera CPUs and the continued growth of Blackwell Ultra. Shipments of Data Center Hopper products to China during the quarter were $2.4 billion. Edge Computing revenue for the third quarter was $8.2 billion, up 42% from a year ago and up 14% sequentially. Strong Blackwell workstation sales and edge compute for Physical AI applications drove the increases, while higher memory and system prices continue to affect consumer PC demand. Gross Margin GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins for the third quarter increased from a year ago on improved mix from Blackwell Ultra. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins decreased slightly sequentially, reflecting the initial Rubin ramp. Expenses GAAP operating expenses for the third quarter were up 57% from a year ago and up 9% sequentially, and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 52% from a year ago and up 7% sequentially. These increases were driven by higher compute infrastructure and employee compensation and benefits costs. Other Income, Net and Income Tax GAAP other income, net includes equity securities gains or losses, interest income, interest expense, and other income and expense. Non-GAAP other income, net excludes equity securities gains or losses and certain other income and expense. Net gains from equity securities for the third quarter were $1.8 billion, comprised of net gains of $2.8 billion from our publicly held equity securities and a net loss of $1.0 billion from our non-marketable equity securities, including impairment of $1.8 billion. GAAP effective tax rate for the third quarter was 17.4%, an increase from a year ago, primarily due to higher revenue. Non-GAAP effective tax rate for the third quarter was 17.0%. Commitments We have entered into strategic commitments across our supply, infrastructure, and partner ecosystems to capitalize on future growth opportunities and support our business. We’ve partnered with our extensive network of suppliers to secure the critical components needed to meet demand for the next several years. Our supply commitments increased from $279 billion last quarter to $390 billion, primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply. Our cloud service agreements and data center lease commitments together of $102 billion, an increase from last quarter’s $74 billion, provide the physical and cloud infrastructure that powers our research and development — from the engineering, product design, and testing of our compute chips, networking products, and systems, to the development of our open models, such as NVIDIA Nemotron™, NVIDIA Cosmos™, and GR00T, and our autonomous vehicle software. Our upcoming data center leases have terms up to twenty years and have not commenced. These leases are expected to commence between the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2033. We may assign some of these leases to third parties in the future. Our equity investments are focused on frontier labs, infrastructure financiers, and other private companies, subject to certain contingencies. Neoclouds and frontier labs are seeing extraordinary demand for AI infrastructure, yet many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support. In response, we have entered into arrangements that help select customers secure the land, power and data center capacity needed to support their growth. We will focus on exceptional sites where visible, durable demand can support multiple generations of NVIDIA compute. We have partnered with leading neoclouds to enable broader access to our AI infrastructure to serve AI startups, model builders, enterprises, research organizations and sovereign customers. Our commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us. The maximum commitment presented assumes these contingencies are satisfactorily resolved. If they are not timely resolved, the amount and timing of our commitments may be affected, and certain commitments could be reduced or eliminated. Under these agreements, we will earn revenue on the upfront sale of our infrastructure and if certain criteria are met, we will participate in revenue share generated by the neoclouds from their third-party customers. In August 2026, we entered into guarantees to provide credit support on the land, power, and shell buildout to secure approximately 4.25 gigawatts (GW) across nine buildings at SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, which will exclusively host NVIDIA infrastructure under 20-year leases to OpenAI, subject to limited exceptions. Our guarantees take effect phase by phase, with each one becoming effective only when its related building is completed and ready for service. The first is expected in fiscal 2029. Our exposure therefore builds over time as each building comes online, up to a maximum of $105 billion, and then declines over each 20-year lease term as OpenAI makes lease payments. We also have the option to provide credit support in phases for approximately 3.8 additional GW as the site scales. To date, we have not made any payments related to our guarantees.
